summary: India localization for Business Central 29. It covers GST (including cess, reverse charge, advance payments, ISD, settlement, reconciliation, e-invoice, e-way bill), TDS and TCS, voucher interface, gate entry, subcontracting, FA depreciation by block and shift, charge assignment and stale cheques. It answers how Indian tax and compliance features are built and set up.
overview:
The India layer is almost entirely its own objects: 1262 added objects and no changes to W1 objects. It is built on a tax engine: codeunits set up GST, Cess, TDS and TCS tax types and use cases (for example "GST Use Case Config", "Cess Tax Type Setup", "Import GST Use Case"). Domain extensions then add GST fields, pages and posting logic to sales, purchase, service, inventory, bank, fixed assets and pricing.

Main capabilities are GST on sales, purchases, services, transfers, journals and bank charges, with reverse charge, import, SEZ, export and exempted cases. Further features are GST settlement, input tax credit adjustments, input service distribution, GSTR-2A reconciliation, e-invoice and e-way bill, TDS and TCS, charge groups, gate entry, subcontracting with delivery challans, income tax depreciation, voucher interface with narrations and stale cheques.

Microsoft Learn documents these on the India local functionality pages: setup of GST, cess, TCS, gate entry, subcontracting, fixed asset depreciation and stale cheques, plus step-by-step transaction scenarios with general ledger entry examples.
key_points: GST engine: tax types, use cases and datasets per area (sales, purchase, service, stock, payments), with CGST, SGST/UTGST, IGST and compensation cess.
GST scenarios: registered and unregistered parties, reverse charge, import, SEZ, export, exempted and composite vendors, advance payments, bank charges and service transfers.
GST settlement, credit adjustment journal, input service distribution, GSTR-2A reconciliation and GST liability for overdue subcontracting challans.
E-invoice (JSON, IRN) for sales and service documents, and e-way bill export to Excel.
TDS and TCS setup, calculation and payment to government authorities, including TCS under section 206C(1H).
Gate entry (inward and outward, posted) linked to purchase, sales, transfer and return documents, plus subcontracting posting and delivery challan application.
Fixed asset depreciation by block, shift and additional depreciation, with an income tax depreciation book.
Voucher interface (six voucher types), narrations, Day Book, Bank Book, Cash Book, Ledger and Voucher Register reports, and stale cheque handling.

areas.what: Core of the localization: GST, Cess, TDS and TCS tax types, use cases and configuration codeunits, GST posting, settlement, journals, distribution, reconciliation, e-invoice and charge handling. Mostly new codeunits, tables, pages and queries.
areas.why: Learn documents GST setup, settlement of net payment liability, credit adjustments, input service distribution, reconciliation with GSTR-2A, e-invoice, e-way bill, TDS and TCS payment.

areas.what: Page and table extensions add GST fields to customers, sales documents, archives, statistics and finance charge memos. Posting and validation logic sits in the Finance codeunits.
areas.why: Learn covers sales to registered and unregistered customers, exports, exempted sales, returns, and TCS on sales.

areas.what: Extensions add GST vendor type, reverse charge, credit availment and charge group fields to vendors and purchase documents, archives and statistics.
areas.why: Learn documents purchases from registered, unregistered, SEZ, composite and foreign vendors, with returns and credit memos.

areas.what: Gate entry feature: inward and outward gate entries, posted versions, comments and attachments, with posting codeunits, a Gate Entry report and warehouse receipt extensions.
areas.why: Learn explains setting up gate entry tracking and attaching inward and outward entries to purchase, sales, transfer and return documents.

areas.what: Voucher interface with posting setup, debit and credit accounts and posted narration, plus Day Book, Bank Book, Cash Book, Ledger, Voucher Register and Check reports. Bank account extensions add GST and stale cheque fields.
areas.why: Learn describes six voucher types and the stale cheque setup, and GST on bank charges.

areas.what: Income tax depreciation with FA blocks, shifts and accounting periods, new depreciation calculation and fiscal year codeunits, and extensions on fixed asset and depreciation book objects.
areas.why: Learn documents block, additional and shift-based depreciation and its setup.

areas.what: GST fields added through table and page extensions on service orders, invoices, credit memos, shipments, contracts and archives.
areas.why: Learn covers GST on service orders, invoices and credit memos.

areas.what: GST fields on items, item charges, locations and inventory setup, plus extensions supporting gate entry on transfer documents and subcontracting on item journals.
Extensions on company information, source code setup and shipping agents to hold GST, TDS, TCS and voucher settings.
Three import codeunits load GST, TDS and TCS use cases into the tax engine.
Subcontracting extensions on production order lines and components, supporting job work with delivery challans.
areas.why: Learn covers subcontracting setup and GST liability for overdue delivery challans.

areas.what: GST fields on price list lines and price worksheet lines.
GST fields added to the resource table and resource card.
A QR Generator codeunit and a .NET component, used for QR codes on e-invoice documents.
A permission set extension for India TDS added to D365 BASIC.

issues: Minor: TDS setup has no dedicated Learn page in the input; the claim is still supported by the Import TDS Use Case codeunit and the Learn pages on TDS calculation and payment.
Minor: audit trail and edit logs (a Learn page and listed on the India overview page) are not mentioned; this is an omission, not an error.

Minor: the overview says domain extensions add GST fields while the code summary shows fields_added 0; this is consistent because the fields come through the 150 India table extensions, not through changes to W1 objects.
